Artigo científico · 2026

Wave and vibration attenuation via full band gaps in 3D periodic sandwich metapanels

Sales, M. B. M.; Araujo, B. C. C.; Santos, M. C. P.; Pereira, F. N.; Miranda Jr., E. J. P.

Journal of the Brazilian Society of Mechanical Sciences and Engineering · v. 48 · 309

Ver publicação ↗

Abstract

Although the concept of metastructures is widely applied for vibration attenuation, the influence of the complexity of the geometry of three-dimensional (3D) panel elements remains a significant gap in the literature. This study investigates the formation of full band gaps in metapanels with a square lattice core in vacuum, considering variations in geometry and polymeric materials. The investigation uses COMSOL Multiphysics and the finite element method. The results show that vacuum and material selection strongly influence full band gaps, particularly in complex 3D configurations. Full band gaps occur only when the core and plates have equal thicknesses, while denser polymers in the core and less dense polymers in the plates increase bandwidth. The study demonstrates passive control of waves and vibrations through periodicity, geometry, and local resonance, without adding inclusions or resonant elements.
